name: Proof Lockup
job: Greet a cold reader with the two to four proofs behind a claim, each a figure they can check, between one short framing line and the promise it buys them.

anatomy.role: Optional framing line above the panel, italic body size, never headline size
One raised box holding every cell (not a card per proof); glass when the page defines it, surface otherwise

One proof; cells split by hairline keylines and aligned on a shared subgrid (label, figure, caption rows line up). Stacked under 30rem of the part's own width, 2 by 2 from 30rem, side by side from 48rem

Mono tabular figure, the one thing the eye lands on; scales with the part's width and never passes the display step: about 1.6rem side by side in an 840px lane, never under the display floor of 1.5rem
Where the figure comes from, one step under body so it does not compete with the kicker and closer
Optional semibold line under the panel: what the reader gets

states.name: Three cells, panel only
states.note: In a column under 30rem, like this one, the cells stack; 2 by 2 from 30rem, side by side from 48rem.

states.name: Phone width
states.note: Below 30rem of its own width the cells stack, split by horizontal keylines.

use_when: The top of an overview needs the why-me in one look: two to four proofs, each a sourced figure.
The same facts would otherwise appear twice, once as a lede paragraph and once as stat tiles; this replaces both.
avoid_when: Do not use it for a figure without a source on the page; a proof with nothing behind it is decoration.
Do not use it for five or more facts, or for a dashboard of live counts; that is the fact tiles or a table.

data.note: One or two sentences. Body size, italic.
Two to four. `fig` is short: a count, a range, "n of m".

access: Cells are a real `ul` of `li`, so a screen reader announces how many proofs there are; each reads label, figure, caption in source order; put whitespace (or block elements) between the three, or some readers run them together.
Meaning never rides on colour: the figure is cyan and also the largest mono text in its cell.
Layout is a container query on the part itself, so it is correct in any column; tracks use `minmax(0, 1fr)` and figures wrap anywhere rather than overflow.

used_by.name: Gravity candidate page overview (gravity.arcs.care), replacing the lede paragraph and the four fact tiles; wired by the page's own session on PR 2219

gates: `kit_specimen.py --check` (in scripts): this page matches its spec.
`kit_primitive_sync.py --check`: every page that marks this block carries it line for line.
`artifact_wrap_lint.py` and `page_gate.py` on every page that carries it; sweep 360 to 1440, including 700 to 1000.
